U039: how to score point-in-time QA — answer content, citation validity, or both. This is a construct-definition question. I should resolve it by arguing both should be reported, with the primary metric being... Let me look at what the literature does:
- TempFinRAG: primary metric answer accuracy; leakage as separate. So it reports both.
- LEGAL-LINK-EU: "a new benchmark that encodes temporal validity" — the labels encode validity of provisions, so correctness includes whether the provision is in force (i.e., validity is part of the label, not just content).
- Legal review: detection criterion "can the system return the text that was in force at T" — scoring is version-identity based, not content equivalence. Also the review says versioned granularity etc.
- SituatedQA: answers scored against context-specific gold answers (content, context-specific) — so content scoring but with context-specific gold, which means the "content" is evaluated relative to the context; if the model answers the current answer instead of the as-of answer, it's wrong. That is content-based but sensitive to version differences.

So the resolution: report both, but make the version-identity (citation validity) the primary for retrieval-level claims, and answer content on the answer-differential subset for answer-level claims. Specifically: the benchmark's retrieval metric must be version-identity (in-force at T), because that's the criterion the legal framework prescribes and because content equivalence can mask contamination; the end-to-end claim must use accuracy on the answer-differential subset because content-based accuracy on non-divergent queries cannot detect harm. So: both, with each attached to a different claim; never a single aggregate.

I should also note the risk: reporting both risks a "two chances to win" concern; mitigate by pre-registering which is primary for which claim.

input.statement: Resolution of U039: neither definition should be discarded, but they must be matched to different claims rather than averaged into one score. Retrieval-level claims - whether a retriever resolves version ambiguity - are scored by version identity, that is, whether the returned passage was in force at the target date, because that is the criterion legal analysis prescribes and what a legal benchmark encoding temporal validity measures; content scoring cannot detect contamination when successive versions share wording. End-to-end claims about user-visible harm are scored by answer accuracy restricted to the answer-differential stratum, because only there can a wrong version change the answer. Consequences: report the contamination rate, the screen pass rate and the conditional accuracy together, never a single aggregate; state in advance which metric adjudicates which claim so the dual reporting cannot be read as metric-shopping; and expect the two definitions to yield different magnitudes, with citation-validity failure more frequent than content failure. A residual definitional question arises for versions whose text is unchanged, where version-identity scoring would penalize retrieving an equivalent passage.

input.description: Combine the recency-decoupled query design with a claim-matched outcome hierarchy. Walk each clause's amendment chain and sample target dates inside each version's validity interval, including a deliberately oversampled stratum whose gold in-force version is not the latest, with gold assigned by version identity. Scoring is matched to the claim rather than averaged: (1) for retrieval-level claims, primary outcome is version-level temporal contamination and version confusion, scored as whether the returned passage was in force at the target date; (2) for end-to-end claims, co-primary outcome is answer accuracy restricted to the answer-differential stratum, where retrieving a non-gold version yields a different reference answer; (3) diagnostic outcomes are citation-validity failure rate scored independently of answer content, plus nDCG/recall and abstention. Report the screen pass rate, per-stratum results, and the pre-registered rule stating which metric adjudicates which claim; always include a recency-only baseline; and report the contamination-to-content-error ratio so the two definitions cannot be conflated.
input.expected_benefit: Makes the claim identifiable and the two harm channels separable: on the non-latest stratum a recency prior cannot win by construction; version-identity labels avoid the confound that identical wording yields identical answers; the answer-differential pass rate quantifies how often version confusion can change a user-visible answer; and pre-registering which metric adjudicates which claim prevents dual reporting from being read as metric-shopping while keeping both the retrieval-level and user-visible failures visible.
input.implementation_difficulty_basis: Contamination and confusion are rules over retrieved passage ids, validity intervals and query strata; the answer-differential screen can be automated with a fixed reader plus spot checks; citation-validity scoring is a second independent rule over the same retrieved ids.
input.experimental_difficulty_basis: Requires amendment chains with usable validity intervals, enough non-latest gold queries for power, a per-version reference answer before the screen can be applied, and pre-registration of the metric-to-claim mapping; the metric computations themselves are simple.
input.main_risk: The non-latest stratum may be too small even after oversampling, or most query-version pairs may fail the answer-differential screen, reducing the result to a metric-level finding; conversely, version-identity scoring may count immaterial version differences - versions whose text is unchanged - as failures, inflating the retrieval-level metric.

input.technical_mechanism: For each clause version chain, derive validity intervals from amendment metadata and construct queries at sampled target dates inside each interval; label gold by version identity. Tag retrieved passages as in-force, superseded or not-yet-in-force relative to the target date and compute contamination/confusion for all queries. Separately, obtain a reference answer per candidate version with a fixed reader; mark queries answer-differential if the gold version's answer differs from at least one competing version's answer, and evaluate answer accuracy only on that subset, reporting the pass rate. Score citation validity as an independent rule on the same retrieved ids so a content-matching but out-of-force citation still counts as a retrieval failure. This modification makes both the version-selection error and the conditions under which it matters part of the measured design, and separates citation validity from answer content so the two harm channels are never merged into one number.
